findings.description: User-spec includes implementation details (RSS, Graph API, HTML parsing) and three fallback methods, which increases complexity and maintenance burden.
findings.suggestion: Simplify to primary method (Graph API if token available, else RSS) and keep HTML parsing as last resort; move implementation details to tech-spec.

findings.description: Graph API integration requires Facebook developer token and app review, which may be a barrier.
findings.suggestion: Verify token availability and consider using RSS generation service as fallback.

findings.description: Could use third-party RSS bridge (e.g., RSS.app) to convert Facebook page to RSS, simplifying integration.
findings.suggestion: Research availability of RSS feed via third-party services before implementing Graph API.

findings.description: Facebook HTML parsing is fragile and may break with UI changes; Graph API rate limits and token expiration could cause integration failures.
findings.suggestion: Implement robust monitoring, rate limiting, and alerting; consider using external service.

alternative_approaches: Consider using RSS feed generated by third-party services (e.g., RSS.app, FetchRSS) to avoid Graph API complexity. Alternatively, use unofficial library facebook-scraper for lightweight scraping. Evaluate if Facebook page still provides RSS via /feeds/page.php?format=atom&id=... If RSS is reliable, implement only RSS parsing and fallback to Graph API only if RSS fails.
integration_risks: Facebook Graph API rate limits (200 requests/hour) may be exceeded if bot runs frequently. Token expiration/revocation could break integration. HTML parsing is fragile and may break with Facebook UI changes. IP blocking risk if using HTML scraping without rate limits. Mitigation: implement rate limiting, token refresh mechanism, monitor errors, and have fallback to admin notification.
summary: The user-spec is feasible and addresses edge cases, but could be simplified to reduce overengineering. Overall status: approved with recommendations.
